mapping_rule_applied: The mapping rule the ais terms record quotes (fixtures/ais/spec/ais_terms.json): a standard or data service the publisher states is a free public offering of a public body -> PUBLIC_GOVERNMENT; an open licence released by its author -> OPEN. Applied: BarentsWatch is a service of the Norwegian state publishing the Norwegian Coastal Administration's AIS data, its terms page names the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) and requires a credit, and the API documentation is a free public page. Two readings fit (NLOD is an open licence, so OPEN is defensible); the government-publisher reading is the one this package's precedents for agency data services take (ndbc_stdmet, coops_csv, airnow_hourly), and it is the one recorded. Both readings are stated here so a later ruling can take the other without re-reading the pages.
not_committed: This record is a reading of the publisher's pages, not an acquisition and not a pin: no document was downloaded into this repository, no hash of any page is claimed, and no clause is transcribed beyond the quoted sentences below. It states no permission: where a page is silent, the record says so rather than inferring a grant. It does not claim the pages still read this way after read_at; a later reading is a later record beside this one. The pages name NLOD without a version number, and this record does not supply one.

standards.name: Terms of Use of the data from BarentsWatch (published 29 July 2016, last updated 02 November 2023 as the page states)
standards.notes: The page continues '... unless API documentation specify otherwise' and states that content demanding special access is not licensed by NLOD; the historic AIS track endpoint's page states no other licence. The credit is required in both languages, 'Data delivered by BarentsWatch' and 'Data levert av BarentsWatch'; the adapter writes the English form at attributes.attribution.
